implementation_notes: TypeScript expresses immutability in the type system: readonly marks properties and index signatures, Readonly<T> maps all top-level properties to their readonly form, ReadonlyArray<T> / readonly T[] remove the mutating members from the type, and as const infers the narrowest fully readonly literal type. The guarantee is erased at runtime and shallow, and readonly does not survive assignment compatibility, so the pattern still rests on the discipline of never mutating plus copying for updates (spread, map, filter). Object.freeze is the runtime complement; the classic private-state class remains the form when the value must be enforced at runtime as well.
pitfalls: readonly is erased and shallow: it stops assignment through that view only, nested objects stay writable, and a readonly array is structurally assignable to a mutable parameter, so an alias can still mutate the value.
Freezing at runtime and typing as readonly are independent: Object.freeze returns Readonly<T> but freezes nothing, and a Readonly<T>-typed value may still be mutable to untyped JavaScript.
Structural typing makes the guarantee non-nominal: any object of the right shape satisfies Readonly<Order>, so values from JSON.parse or an HTTP client are read-only by convention only.

variants.name: Object.freeze typed as Readonly<T>
variants.implementation_notes: Where the value must actually resist mutation - a library surface, a plugin boundary, shared state - pair the type with a runtime freeze in the factory: return the object typed as Readonly<T> (or ReadonlyArray<T>) after calling Object.freeze on it and on its nested structures. Freeze is shallow and silent in sloppy-mode code, so only frozen factories should construct values and the deep case needs an explicit recursive freeze with cycle handling.
pitfalls: Freeze is shallow: nested objects and arrays must be frozen explicitly, and a recursive deepFreeze has to handle cycles (a function's prototype points back to the function).
Writes to a frozen object fail silently in sloppy mode, so frozen values must flow through strict-mode code (modules) where the violation throws instead of corrupting assumptions.
